description: The base for every Forever Works repo: weekly dependency PRs, and the ones that stay within a major line merge on their own once every check on them has passed.

Renovate merges them itself, never through GitHub's auto-merge (platformAutomerge off): it merges only when every check on the branch has passed, so a branch with no checks, or with a pending or red one, waits for a person.

Majors wait on the Dependency Dashboard for a tick and then stay a PR for a person; so do 0.x npm packages, which semver lets break in a minor. A security fix within a major line merges the same way, without the weekly wait.
npm minors and patches arrive as one weekly PR, three days after release; GitHub Actions as another, three days after release and pinned to commit SHAs.
Commits by github-actions[bot] on a Renovate branch (a fix workflow's) do not stop Renovate from rebasing it.

packageRules.description: A new npm release waits three days before Renovate proposes it, so a bad release has time to be noticed and pulled.

A new Action release, a moved tag included, waits three days before Renovate proposes it: an Action runs with the workflow's token and secrets, and a bad release is usually withdrawn within that time.
Our own reusable workflows (expo-fix) are called at @main on purpose, so every repo runs the current one: they are not pinned to a commit.
Every npm minor and patch in one weekly PR.
Every GitHub Action in one weekly PR.

description: An update within a major line merges on its own once every check on its PR has passed: Renovate checks the branch on each run and merges only when nothing is pending or red.
A branch with no checks at all, or with any check pending or red, never merges this way (ignoreTests stays false).
A 0.x npm package promises nothing between minors, so its updates come as their own weekly PR for a person.
They are grouped apart so that one of them does not hold back the automerge of every other npm minor and patch.

packageRules.description: A major stays a PR for a person, after its tick on the Dependency Dashboard.
